newsitem.title: GREECE: BASKETBALL-PANATHINAIKOS BEAT OLIMPIJA IN EURO LEAGUE DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-PANATHINAIKOS BEAT OLIMPIJA IN EURO LEAGUE DEBUT.

text.p: Holders Panathinaikos made a winning debut in the revamped European clubs' basketball championship on Wednesday beating Slovenia's Olimpija Ljubljana 75-67 in a group C qualifying clash.
It was the first test for Panathinaikos' totally new team after last season's triumph in the Final Four tournament in Paris which earned them their first European championship title.

Despite a nervous first half which they finished with a slender 30-29 lead, the Greeks had the upper hand throughout the match. They had a 58 percent shooting average and dominated the boards with Spanish forward Feran Martinez sinking 18 points and pulling down 12 rebounds.
Greek guard Frangiskos Alvertis contributed 13 points and team captain Nikos Economou added 11.
Olimpija, also boasting a new team, put up a fight midway through the second half when Panathinaikos took an average eight point advantage and never looked back.
Power forward Marian Kraljevic had 15 points for the Slovenians and American guard Daren Henry added 13.

"We are just started the season and played without our main forward (NBA player John Salley) who will join the team next week. We will certainly play better in the future," Panathinaikos president Pavlos Yannakopoulos told reporters.
Panathinaikos face Spain's Barcelona next week. The two teams crossed swords in the final last season and share the role of favourites this season.
The new European basketball league consists of four groups of six clubs, instead of two of eight.
